import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Mahler's 3/2 Problem

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahler%27s_3/2_problem)
-/

namespace Mahler32

/-- For a real number `α`, define `Ω(α)` as
$$
\Omega (\alpha )=\inf _{\theta > 0}\left({\limsup _{n\rightarrow \infty }\left\lbrace
{\theta \alpha ^{n}}\right\rbrace -\liminf _{n\rightarrow \infty }\left\lbrace {\theta \alpha ^{n}}\right\rbrace }\right).
$$
-/
noncomputable def Ω (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sInf {Filter.atTop.limsup (fun n ↦ Int.fract (θ * α ^ n))
    - Filter.atTop.liminf (fun n ↦ Int.fract (θ * α ^ n)) | (θ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < θ)}

/-- The **Mahler Conjecture** states that there are no Z-numbers. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem mahler_conjecture (x : ℝ) (hx : IsZNumber x) : False := by
  sorry

/-- If Mahler's conjecture is true, i.e. there are no Z-numbers, then `Ω(3/2)` exceeds `1/2`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem mahler_conjecture.variants.consequence (H : type_of% mahler_conjecture) :
    1 / 2 < Ω (3 / 2) := by
  sorry

/-- It is known that for all rational `p/q > 1` in lowest terms, we have `Ω(p/q) > 1/p`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem mahler_conjecture.variants.flatto_lagarias_pollington (p q : ℕ) (hq : 1 < q)
    (hpq : p.Coprime q) (hpq' : q < p) : 1 / p < Ω (p / q) := by
  sorry

end Mahler32

findings.description: The implication is reversed. `type_of% mahler_conjecture` elaborates to `∀ x : ℝ, IsZNumber x → False`, so this declaration asserts that nonexistence of Z-numbers implies `Ω(3/2) > 1/2`. The source instead gives this bound as a sufficient condition for nonexistence. These are opposite implications, not contrapositives. The source's direction follows because a Z-number x gives limsup at most 1/2 and liminf at least 0, hence Ω(3/2) ≤ 1/2. I proved that direction in Lean without using any admitted theorem.
findings.source_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahler%27s_3/2_problem explicitly says: “Mahler's conjecture would follow if Ω(3/2) exceeds 1/2.”
findings.suggested_fix: Reverse the hypothesis and conclusion: `theorem mahler_conjecture.variants.consequence (H : 1 / 2 < Ω (3 / 2)) : type_of% mahler_conjecture := by ...`. Update the docstring to describe the bound as implying Mahler's conjecture.

findings.description: The strict conclusion `1 / p < Ω (p / q)` strengthens the named primary result, which only asserts `1 / p ≤ Ω (p / q)`. The Lean faithfully copies Wikipedia's displayed strict inequality, but that display misquotes its cited paper. The distinction matters: the strict infimum bound requires a positive gap above 1/p uniform over every positive multiplier, whereas the primary theorem permits equality. This finding concerns the mismatch with the cited result, not a claim that the strict strengthening has been disproved.
findings.source_evidence: Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington, “On the range of fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n},” Acta Arithmetica 70 (1995), Theorem 1.4, p. 129, gives `limsup − liminf ≥ 1/p` for every positive ξ. Page 130 explicitly restates it as “Theorem 1.4 asserts that Ω(p/q) ≥ 1/p.” Section 3, p. 138, also notes an unresolved endpoint-related strengthening. DOI: https://doi.org/10.4064/aa-70-2-125-147 ; full text: https://www.impan.pl/shop/publication/transaction/download/product/108521?download.pdf .
findings.suggested_fix: Change the conclusion to `1 / p ≤ Ω (p / q)`, correct the inequality in the docstring, and cite Theorem 1.4 of the primary paper directly.

findings.description: The docstring says “all rational p/q > 1 in lowest terms,” but the Lean correctly assumes `hq : 1 < q`. The prose therefore includes integers p/1, for which the claimed positive lower bound fails even after changing it to a non-strict bound: choosing θ = 1 gives zero fractional parts at every index, and Ω(p) = 0. I proved Ω(k) = 0 for natural k in Lean, including the counterexample p = 2, q = 1 to the unrestricted prose.
findings.source_evidence: The primary paper's introduction, p. 126, explicitly restricts attention to non-integer rationals. Theorem 1.4 begins “Let p > q ≥ 2 be relatively prime integers.” https://doi.org/10.4064/aa-70-2-125-147 . The file's docstring omits the denominator restriction present in both this primary statement and the Lean hypotheses.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `q > 1` to the docstring, or say “non-integral rational p/q > 1 in lowest terms.” Retain the existing `hq` hypothesis.

reformulations.difference: Mahler's original paper imposes the fractional-part condition for n ≥ 0, while the imported `IsZNumber` imposes it only for n ≥ 1, agreeing with Wikipedia. The global nonexistence statement is nevertheless equivalent.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A positive witness satisfying the condition for all n ≥ 0 also satisfies it for n ≥ 1. Conversely, if x satisfies it for n ≥ 1, then y = (3/2)x > 0 satisfies it for all n ≥ 0, since y(3/2)^n = x(3/2)^(n+1). Thus existence, and therefore nonexistence, is equivalent under the two conventions. Proved as `Review.no_znumber_iff_original` in `/workspace/review/equivalence.lean`.

sources_consulted: K. Mahler, “An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2,” Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society 8 (1968), 313–321: https://doi.org/10.1017/S1446788700005371
L. Flatto, J. C. Lagarias and A. D. Pollington, “On the range of fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n},” Acta Arithmetica 70 (1995), 125–147: https://doi.org/10.4064/aa-70-2-125-147
review.notes: Checked all four declarations and the imported IsZNumber definition. Lean confirms natural-number exponents and real, not natural, division. The fractional-part sequences are bounded in [0,1], their limsup-minus-liminf values lie in [0,1], and the set defining Ω is nonempty and bounded below; no default-value defect arises. Experiments in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, `bounds.lean`, and `equivalence.lean` compile successfully. The corrected implication and boundary/equivalence proofs have no `sorryAx` dependency. No separate status discrepancy was found; the main conjecture remains presented as open by the consulted sources.

submission.summary: Reversed the conditional so that Ω(3/2) > 1/2 implies nonexistence of Z-numbers. Changed the FLP bound to Ω(p/q) ≥ 1/p, updated both docstrings, included the denominator restriction, and cited the primary paper’s Theorem 1.4. Only Mahler32.lean was edited; the requested compile command succeeds with only the permitted `sorry` warnings.
